subject: Auditlog handover: residency windows & export formats
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.org>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, procurement@acmehealth.org
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log export request — residency / formats

Hi Diego,

Following up from our compliance checklist call: Acme needs an official description of how Redwood exports audit/access logs for customers in the US. Specifically we need answers to:

- What export formats are available (CSV/JSON/Parquet)?
- Maximum retention you can export from (hosted & dedicated/private).
- Can exports include full event payloads, IP addresses, and unredacted user ids?
- Delivery options: S3 push to our bucket, direct download, or physical handover?
- Typical time window for a bulk export (start -> completion).

We have an internal deadline for evidence by 11/10. If you can send a short runbook and sample export schema that would be great.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Compliance
Acme Health

Attachment: acme-export-request.csv (fields list)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.org>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export request — residency / formats

Elena — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR below and a short playbook attached.

- Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), CSV, and Parquet are supported. We recommend Parquet for large exports for space and schema preservation.
- Retention windows: Hosted tenants: up to 90 days retained in the standard audit index (self-serve). For customers on Dedicated we can retain up to 365 days by configuration; Private (on-prem/VPC) is customer-determined.
- Payloads: Exports include full event payloads by default for system events. User identifiers can be exported as full IDs, but we provide hashing/pseudonymization on request (SHA-256 salt per-tenant) and IP address redaction if required.
- Delivery: Primary delivery is push to a customer-owned S3 bucket (us-east-1 / us-west-2 / eu-west-1). We also support an encrypted HTTPS bundle download (expires 7 days). Physical handover (disk shipment) is possible for Private/Dedicated after PO and compliance sign-off — that path is slower and involves on-site verification.
- Timing: Typical bulk export for a 90-day audit log (50GB compressed) completes within 24-72 hours from request acceptance. For longer windows or larger volumes expect 72-120 hours.

I attached our export option table (audit-export-options.csv) and a one-page runbook. Two notes: exports are immutable snapshots taken at request time (we include an export manifest with checksums). Also, for GDPR/CCPA deletion requests we can generate an export snapshot prior to deletion as part of the workflow.

Let me know if you want us to push a test export to your S3; if so, send bucket name, region, and an IAM role ARN we can assume (we will only write to the specified prefix).

Diego — adding a legal/compliance note for the thread.

- If Acme requests exports containing PII or user-identifiable data we need a signed DPA amendment / export Addendum. Please flag whether the export will include raw user identifiers or whether Acme prefers pseudonymized identifiers.
- For S3 pushes to customer buckets, confirm whether Acme's bucket enforces server-side encryption and the required KMS key. We will only assume the role if the bucket policy explicitly limits write access to the expected prefix.
- Deletion/retention: if Acme requests us to delete logs from hosted storage after export, that deletion is performed within 7 business days after export receipt confirmation unless there is a legal hold.

Diego — can you confirm the default manifest fields (timestamp, event_type, actor_id, source_ip, resource_id, request_id)? If we provide an export sample schema I can route to legal for sign-off.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
